s1.syndrome_frame: preterm infant with a large sacrococcygeal mass and signs of hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: large sacrococcygeal mass with mixed solid and cystic components
rapid growth of the mass during pregnancy
severe metabolic acidosis and hemodynamic instability at birth
visible active bleeding from the mass
key_facts: female infant delivered at 26 weeks and 6 days of gestation
sacrococcygeal mass identified on ultrasound at 19 weeks
mass size increased to 60×70×57 mm by 22 weeks
mass had mixed solid and cystic components
normal array comparative genomic hybridization and fetal echocardiogram
birth weight was 1300 g
Apgar scores were 0, 0, and 5 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
required positive-pressure ventilation and intravenous adrenaline
initial vital signs included heart rate 103/min, respiratory rate 70/min, and blood pressure 19/15 mm Hg
physical examination revealed pallor, prolonged capillary refill, and a large sacrococcygeal mass with active bleeding
initial management included transfusion of red blood cells, fresh-frozen plasma, and platelets
severe metabolic acidosis with pH 6.80, HCO₃⁻ 8.6 mmol/L, and base excess −25

shortlist.label: Sacrooccygeal Teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: large sacrococcygeal mass with mixed solid and cystic components, consistent with teratoma

shortlist.label: Neuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: sacrococcygeal mass with rapid growth and signs of hemodynamic instability, possible neuroblastoma

shortlist.label: Yolk Sac Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: sacrococcygeal mass with rapid growth and signs of hemodynamic instability, possible yolk sac tumor

shortlist.label: Embryonal Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: sacrococcygeal mass with rapid growth and signs of hemodynamic instability, possible rhabdomyosarcoma

shortlist.label: Congenital Sacrococcygeal Fibrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: sacrococcygeal mass with rapid growth and signs of hemodynamic instability, possible congenital fibrosarcoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a sacrococcygeal mass with mixed solid and cystic components, identified on ultrasound at 19 weeks and growing rapidly, is consistent with a sacrococcygeal teratoma. The normal array comparative genomic hybridization and fetal echocardiogram also support this diagnosis, as sacrococcygeal teratomas are typically isolated anomalies without associated chromosomal abnormalities or cardiac defects.

rejected.label: Neuroblastoma
rejected.why: Neuroblastoma is less likely given the location and mixed solid and cystic components of the mass, which are more characteristic of sacrococcygeal teratoma.

rejected.label: Yolk Sac Tumor
rejected.why: Yolk sac tumor is a type of germ cell tumor that is more commonly associated with testicular or ovarian masses, rather than sacrococcygeal masses.

rejected.label: Embryonal Rhabdomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma is a type of soft tissue sarcoma that is more commonly associated with head and neck or genitourinary tract masses, rather than sacrococcygeal masses.

rejected.label: Congenital Sacrococcygeal Fibrosarcoma
rejected.why: Congenital sacrococcygeal fibrosarcoma is a rare tumor that can present with a sacrococcygeal mass, but the mixed solid and cystic components and rapid growth of the mass in this case are more characteristic of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
